notes: The Fritzing image was not available, so the breadboard layout is my own. The pin-to-pin connections follow the tutorial text and the code comments.
The AD5206 straddles the centre gap of the breadboard. Pins 1-12 sit in row e of columns 1-12 (bank t). Pins 13-24 sit in row f of columns 12 down to 1 (bank b).
All A pins go to +5V. All B pins go to ground. Each W pin goes through a 220 ohm resistor to an LED anode, and each LED cathode goes to ground.
VDD goes to 5V. VSS and the GND pin go to ground. CS goes to Uno pin 10, SDI to pin 11 and CLK to pin 13, as in the code comments.
Rail tp is +5V and rail tn is ground. Each wire or LED leg uses its own rail hole number. This is only for bookkeeping, because a rail is one strip.
Each W pin uses a jumper wire to a free column, then a resistor, then an LED. Channel 1 is W1 and so on, so channel numbering follows the pin names, not the code's 0-5 addresses.
The AD5206 is not in the catalogue, so I added it as a new part type with 24 lead ports named after its pins.
